title: The Horizon of the Rust Belt
premise: Petra Villalobos, a xenolinguist whose mind has been rewired by decades of contact with the silent Vessic species, ferries messages between a decaying human colony and two rival fleets hovering on the brink of war. When the colony's children begin dreaming identical dreams in a language only Petra can parse, he discovers the Vessic are broadcasting through them — and that the message is a countdown tied to the colony's failing reactor. To prevent annihilation, Petra fabricates a translation, inventing a peace treaty that never existed to keep the fleets apart while he races to decode the real warning. In the end, his lie is exposed, but the truth it bought time for — that both fleets were being manipulated by a third, hidden signal — saves everyone except his reputation, and he chooses exile among the Vessic rather than face what power made of him.
about_author: Rafael Ishikawa is the pen name of a former shipping-log analyst who spent nine years documenting cargo routes between orbital stations before turning to fiction. They write about language, distance, and the people who keep impossible systems running.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Petra Villalobos arrives at Rust Belt Colony aboard a freight hauler, delivering diplomatic dispatches between two hostile fleets. His POV establishes his isolation: he no longer dreams in any human language, and the colony regards him with suspicion. Emotional beat: weary professionalism masking profound loneliness as he realizes the children in the docking bay are humming a rhythm he recognizes from Vessic transmissions.

chapters.title: Children of the Same Sleep
chapters.summary: Colony administrator Dara Okafor, POV, confronts Petra after forty-seven children report identical dreams of a descending spiral. She wants it contained; Petra recognizes linguistic structure no human child could invent. Emotional beat: dread curdling into fascination as Petra transcribes the dream-language and finds it grammatically alive — it is changing between tellings, like a conversation.

chapters.title: Grammar of the Deep
chapters.summary: Petra's POV as he works nights decoding the dream-speech, discovering embedded references to the colony reactor's decay curve — numbers the children could not know. He sends a coded query to the Vessic relay and receives silence. Emotional beat: mounting vertigo as he realizes the dreams aren't a message but a broadcast, and someone is listening on both fleet channels.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Sky
chapters.summary: Fleet liaison Captain Reyes, POV, pressures Petra to declare the dreams either Vessic aggression or fleet propaganda — whichever serves her side. Petra stalls, sensing that any official translation will be weaponized. Emotional beat: the first taste of corruption's mechanics, as Reyes offers him protection, funding, and flattery in exchange for a version of truth shaped to her fleet's advantage.

chapters.title: The Lie That Holds
chapters.summary: Petra, POV, makes his fateful choice: he submits a fabricated translation claiming the Vessic have proposed a formal ceasefire contingent on fleet restraint. Both fleets stand down. The lie works because it is beautiful. Emotional beat: intoxicating relief followed immediately by guilt, as he watches armed ships hold position because of words he invented in a sleepless night.

chapters.title: Countdown in the Walls
chapters.summary: Engineer Tomas Iwu, POV, traces anomalous power draws to the reactor core and finds its failure timeline matches the numbers buried in the children's dreams exactly. The reactor will breach in nineteen days. Emotional beat: cold horror as Tomas realizes the dreams weren't a threat — they were a warning, and the man who translated them said otherwise.

chapters.title: What the Children Knew
chapters.summary: Petra interrogates his own fabrication, cross-referencing the true dream-text against his invented treaty. The real message describes not an attack but an evacuation protocol — the Vessic were offering rescue capacity if the colony acted fast. Emotional beat: shame sharpening into resolve; Petra must now sustain his lie long enough to redirect both fleets toward evacuation instead of war.

chapters.title: The Unraveling
chapters.summary: Reyes, POV, discovers discrepancies in Petra's translation archives and confronts him privately — not with arrest, but with blackmail: translate the war declaration she needs, or the fleets learn their ceasefire was fiction. Emotional beat: the theme crystallizes; Petra sees clearly how power corrupts, because he has already corrupted himself, and she is simply offering him the mirror.

chapters.title: Nineteen Days Short
chapters.summary: Climax. With the reactor at critical threshold, Petra broadcasts everything — his forgery, the true dream-text, the Vessic evacuation offer — to both fleets simultaneously, gambling that shared truth lands harder than managed lies. Fleets scramble not to fight each other but to evacuate. Emotional beat: cathartic terror and release as the reactor breaches harmlessly into evacuated space, and Petra stands exposed, ruined, and finally honest.

chapters.title: Exile Among Listeners
chapters.summary: Resolution. Petra declines repatriation and boards a Vessic vessel, leaving Dara a final letter explaining that justice sometimes lives outside law, and loyalty to truth cost him every other loyalty. The children wave from the docks, still dreaming, now gently. Emotional beat: bittersweet peace — he lost his world but kept his integrity, and somewhere in the dark, something patient begins teaching him to dream again.
